premise: A diocesan finance auditor investigates missing memorial fund donations at a small-town parish, reconstructing the timeline from donation ledgers, bank deposit batches, and parish council meeting minutes.
setting: Small-town parish and community center — narthex, parish office, finance records room, community hall, and parish council meeting room
investigator_character: Diocesan finance auditor appointed by the parish council to reconcile memorial fund records before the annual review
opening_situation: You arrive at St. Brendan's parish hall to find parish administrator Grace Brennan waiting with a preliminary reconciliation packet. Volunteer bookkeeper Helen Marsh has flagged ledger entries that do not match bank deposits, and council treasurer Rita Santos says meeting minutes allocate funds differently than the ledger shows.
initial_observable_facts: Memorial fund donation ledger totals $18,400 but bank deposit batch shows $14,200.
Parish administrator Grace Brennan prepared the reconciliation packet for your review.
Volunteer bookkeeper Helen Marsh noticed white-out corrections on ledger page 47.
Parish council treasurer Rita Santos says minutes allocate memorial funds to stained-glass restoration only.
in_world_duration: one audit day (approximately four in-world hours)
location_scale: single parish campus with five primary locations
content_boundaries: no graphic violence; no supernatural elements; financial fraud and embezzlement themes; no sexual content
required_themes: one perfect ending and several imperfect endings
deadline_or_constraint: Diocesan annual review reconciliation due at 1700; parish council meeting at 1800
author_notes: Codename: The Parish Ledger. Culprit NPC-GRACE diverted memorial fund deposits and altered ledger entries before audit. Emphasis on donation ledger, bank deposits, and meeting minutes — not object theft.
